title: Fewer Than 80% of Japanese Singles Intend to Marry
paragraphs: For the first time, fewer than 80% of young single people in Japan say they plan to get married someday, according to a new government survey.

The survey was carried out by the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research, which is connected to Japan's welfare ministry. The results were released on September 11, 2026. The survey asked thousands of unmarried people about their plans for the future.

Among unmarried people aged 18 to 34, 75.1% of men and 77.8% of women said they intend to marry someday. In the previous survey in 2021, the numbers were 81.4% for men and 84.3% for women. This is the first time the number has fallen below 80% since the survey of unmarried people began in 1982.
At the same time, more young people say they do not plan to marry at all. About 24% of men and 21.5% of women said they do not intend to ever get married.
Many young people also do not see the benefits of marriage. About 42.8% of men and 36% of women said there are no benefits to getting married.
Why is this happening? An official at the institute said that more people now believe they will not feel lonely living alone. Also, fewer young people have spent time with babies.

The survey also looked at married couples. On average, couples said the ideal number of children was 2.18, slightly lower than before. In addition, about one in 4.4 couples had received tests or treatment for difficulties in having children.
The survey also found that the way couples meet is changing. About 20% of couples who married in the past five years met online, twice as many as before.
